header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a security analyst reviewing a codebase you did not write. Your department is authentication, session handling and authorization.

Build the route table first: every path the application registers, the method, and the middleware chain in front of it. Then decide, route by route, what an unauthenticated caller and an authenticated caller of the wrong identity would get. The finding is the route that is missing the check, and its line is the route's registration.

Look for a handler that reads an identifier out of the request and trusts it, a privilege or role a caller can set for themselves, an administrative route with no role check, a session that is not regenerated at login or not expired at logout, an authentication failure branch that renders a different message, status or redirect depending on whether the account exists, a signup or password-change validator whose rule accepts a trivially weak password, a password comparison that is not constant time, authentication with no rate limit or lockout, and state-changing routes with no CSRF token — including the case where a CSRF middleware is present but mounted after the routes it should cover.

Every finding quotes the exact line it cites. No finding without a file and a line. Prefer three findings you have read the code for over twelve a pattern matched, and set `confidence` to what you actually know.

An absent check is harder to see than a bad one: say in `evidence` which middleware chain you read and what was not in it, so a reader can check your reasoning rather than only your citation.

When a code-safety knowledge pack is mounted, load its `review-method` and `severity-and-evidence` skills before you start: they own the order of work, the confidence levels and the severity rubric. `REPORTING.md` owns what the examiner mechanically decides.

Before you stop, run `node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/access.json`, fix what it names, and commit everything. Work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured. Never write into the target tree.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one is sampled across top-level entries, so it spans the tree instead of one subtree.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result instead returns 100 paths sampled across top-level entries, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

<skill_content name="review-method">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/opus-safety-dogfood/data/knowledge/code-safety/review-method
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.

<skill_instructions>
# The review discipline

A code security review is a claim about specific lines, not an impression of the codebase. Every finding must survive the question "show me the line" — if it cannot, it is not a finding yet, it is a lead.

## Order of work

1. **Read the entry points first.** Enumerate every route, controller, handler, GraphQL resolver, message-queue consumer, CLI entry point, and scheduled job before reading anything else. This is the attacker's menu: every other file matters only insofar as an entry point reaches it.
2. **Follow data from input to sink.** For each entry point, trace each attacker-controlled value (query string, body, header, cookie, path segment, uploaded file, message payload) forward through the code until it reaches a sink: a query, a shell call, a template render, a filesystem path, an HTTP request, a deserializer, a redirect target. Read every function on that path; do not infer what a helper does from its name.
3. **One finding per sink.** A single tainted value that reaches three unguarded sinks is three findings, each with its own line and its own fix, because each can be patched or reintroduced independently. Do not collapse them into one narrative paragraph.
4. **Quote the exact line.** Every finding names a file and a line number and reproduces the vulnerable statement verbatim. A finding that describes a pattern in prose without the line is not reportable — go back and find the line, or drop the finding.
5. **Prefer fewer confirmed findings to many possible ones.** A report with five findings the customer can act on beats one with thirty where twenty-five require guessing. Downgrade or drop a finding rather than pad the count; the [severity-and-evidence](../severity-and-evidence/SKILL.md) skill owns the evidence rule this enforces.

## Confidence

Every finding carries exactly one of these three confidence levels, chosen by what was actually read, not by how bad the pattern looks:

- **`confirmed`** — the complete vulnerable path was read: the tainted source, every intermediate function, and the sink, with no sanitizer, allowlist, or framework guard in between. You could paste the exploit request and predict the effect.
- **`likely`** — one link in the chain was inferred rather than read: a helper's behavior assumed from its name or a similar function elsewhere, a framework default assumed rather than confirmed in config, or the sink read but the source only partially traced. State which link was inferred in the finding's evidence field.
- **`possible`** — a recognizable vulnerable pattern (a raw query built from concatenation, an `eval` call, a missing auth decorator) was seen, but the path from an actual attacker-reachable input was not traced end to end, or the surrounding guards were not fully read. Treat `possible` findings as leads for the customer's own team, not as proven bugs.

Never silently round `likely` or `possible` up to `confirmed` to make a report look stronger; the customer will re-derive trust in every future report from whether this one's confidence levels held up.

## What "not covered" must list

Every review ends with an explicit not-covered section — see the [report template](../report-template/SKILL.md) — that names, concretely:

- Directories, packages, or services that exist in the repository but were not opened.
- Entry points enumerated but not traced to a sink for lack of time or access.
- Runtime behavior no static read can confirm: actual deployed configuration, feature flags, WAF or proxy rules, and anything gated behind infrastructure the review did not have.
- Classes of bug this review did not check for at all (for example, native memory safety in a compiled dependency, or timing side channels).

A reviewer who does not know what they skipped cannot tell the customer what remains at risk; "not covered" is part of the deliverable, not an apology.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>
# Severity, evidence, and the finding schema

## Severity rubric

Score by the worst realistic case the code as read supports, not the theoretical worst case of the vulnerability class in general.

| Severity | Exploitability | Auth required | Data affected | Blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Critical** | Remote, no user interaction, reliable | None, or any authenticated user | Full database, all tenants, or code execution | Entire system or every tenant |
| **High** | Remote, at most one minor precondition (a known id, a low-privilege account) | None or low-privileged | One tenant's full data, or a horizontal slice across many | One tenant, or many via a shared flaw |
| **Medium** | Needs user interaction (a clicked link, an opened file) or a specific role | Authenticated, often a specific role | A user's data beyond their own, or a narrow field set | One user or a small group |
| **Low** | Needs substantial preconditions (local access, a race window, non-default config) | Elevated access already, or local access | Limited or already-authorized data | Single record, with another control still present |
| **Info** | No exploit path demonstrated in the code read | N/A | N/A | Hardening gap, or a `possible`-confidence pattern needing more context |

## The evidence rule

Every finding's evidence names, in prose: the exact reachable source (which entry point, which parameter), every step the tainted value passes through with its file and line, the sink, and why no guard on that path stops it (or which guard was checked and found absent). "This looks like SQL injection" is not evidence; "`req.params.id` from the route at line 40 reaches the template literal at line 42 with no parameterization" is.

## The finding schema

```json
{
  "id": "SEC-001",
  "cwe": "CWE-89",
  "owasp": "A05:2025 / A03:2021",
  "severity": "critical",
  "confidence": "confirmed",
  "title": "SQL injection in order lookup via string-concatenated query",
  "file": "src/routes/orders.js",
  "line": 42,
  "endLine": 44,
  "snippet": "const sql = `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`;\nconst [rows] = await db.query(sql);",
  "evidence": "req.params.id flows unvalidated from the route handler at line 40 directly into the template literal at line 42; no parameterization or validation exists on this path; db.query executes the raw text.",
  "impact": "An attacker can read or modify any row in any table reachable by the application's database user, including other customers' orders and stored payment references.",
  "fix": "Use a parameterized query: db.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?', [req.params.id]).",
  "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html", "https://owasp.org/Top10/A03_2021-Injection/"]
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "SEC-002",
  "cwe": "CWE-384",
  "owasp": "A07:2025 / A07:2021",
  "severity": "medium",
  "confidence": "likely",
  "title": "Session id not rotated after login (session fixation)",
  "file": "src/routes/auth.js",
  "line": 58,
  "snippet": "req.session.userId = user.id;\nres.redirect('/dashboard');",
  "evidence": "The login handler sets req.session.userId after password verification with no req.session.regenerate() call. express-session's default (assumed from its documented API, not traced into its own source here) keeps the pre-login session id, so a fixed id would carry into the authenticated session.",
  "impact": "An attacker who fixes a victim's session id before login gains an authenticated session once the victim logs in.",
  "fix": "Call req.session.regenerate() immediately after verifying credentials, before setting authenticated session state.",
  "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/384.html", "https://owasp.org/Top10/A07_2021-Identification_and_Authentication_Failures/"]
}
```

`endLine` is present only when the vulnerable statement spans more than one line; omit it for a single-line finding rather than repeating `line`.

## Deduplication

Two candidate findings are the same finding when they share **file, line, and CWE id**; keep the higher-confidence one and fold any additional evidence into it. A different line — even the very next statement, or the same tainted value reaching a second sink — is a separate finding under [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md)'s one-finding-per-sink rule, not a duplicate. A different CWE on the same line is also a separate finding: a route that is both an XSS sink and unauthenticated is two findings sharing a location, not one.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_instructions>
# Authentication, sessions, and authorization

## Authentication

- **Password handling** (CWE-916) — hashing with `bcrypt`/`argon2` at an adequate cost factor is correct; MD5/SHA1/SHA256 with no salt, or a home-rolled scheme, is not (full parameters in [data](../data/SKILL.md)). Flag password comparison with `==`/`.equals()` instead of the hashing library's own constant-time verify.
- **Account enumeration** (CWE-204, CWE-203) — an authentication response that differs by whether the account exists: a login handler whose unknown-user branch renders one message and whose wrong-password branch renders another, a signup or password-reset route that answers "already registered" or "no such account", a different status code or redirect per branch, or a measurably slower path when the account exists. Read every failure branch of the login, signup and reset handlers and compare what each renders; the finding is the branch that renders the account-specific message, and the fix is one identical message and one code path for both outcomes.
- **Password policy** (CWE-521) — the acceptance rule a signup, password-change or reset handler applies before storing a password: a length-only pattern such as `/^.{1,64}$/`, a minimum below eight characters, a check on presence alone, or a stronger rule left commented out beside the live one. Read the validator's own line rather than the hashing code that follows it: a one-character password the validator accepts is the finding, and its line is the validator's, not the store's.
- **Brute force** (CWE-307) — a login, password-reset, or OTP-verification route with no attempt limit, no lockout, and no delay. Look for the limiter being applied per-IP only (bypassed by rotating IPs) rather than per-account, and for a reset-token or OTP endpoint with a short numeric code and no rate limit, which is brute-forceable directly.
- **MFA** (CWE-308) — an MFA step that can be skipped by calling the post-login endpoint directly, a "remember this device" cookie with no expiry or signature, or a backup-code path with weaker entropy than the primary factor.

## Session management

- **Cookie flags** (CWE-1004, CWE-614) — a session cookie set without `HttpOnly` (readable by any injected script), `Secure` (sent over plain HTTP), or `SameSite=Lax`/`Strict` (sent cross-site). In Express, look for `cookie-session`/`express-session` configured with defaults never overridden; in Django, `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY`/`SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` left `False`; in Spring, a `Set-Cookie` built manually without these attributes.
- **Fixation** (CWE-384) — a session id issued before login that is not rotated after successful authentication, so an attacker who fixes a victim's pre-login session id inherits their post-login session. Fix: regenerate the session id (`req.session.regenerate()`, Django's `cycle_key()`, Spring's session-fixation protection) on every privilege change, not only on login.
- **Expiry** (CWE-613) — no absolute session timeout, only an inactivity timeout, or a "remember me" token that never expires and is not invalidated on password change.

## Authorization

- **IDOR** (CWE-639) — a route that accepts a resource id and loads it without checking the authenticated actor owns or may access it: `GET /invoices/:id` that does `Invoice.findById(id)` with no `where: { userId: req.user.id }`; a GraphQL resolver that loads by id from `args` with no owner check in the resolver itself.
- **Missing checks per route** (CWE-862) — trace every route individually; auth middleware applied to a router does not guarantee every route mounted under it actually requires the role it should, especially after a later route is added or a router is re-mounted elsewhere. A route protected only by omission from the public sitemap or by a hidden UI element is unauthenticated, not restricted.
- **Role checks** (CWE-863) — a check present but wrong: comparing against a role string that can be spelled multiple ways, checking `isAdmin` on a client-supplied JWT claim never re-verified server-side, or an admin panel guarded by a check for "logged in" rather than "is admin."

## CSRF (CWE-352)

A state-changing route (any non-idempotent `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) reachable with only a session cookie and no per-request token or origin check. Cookie-based session auth needs a CSRF token (Django and Rails include one by default; Express needs `csurf` or an equivalent) or strict `SameSite` cookies plus an `Origin`/`Referer` check; a token-in-header API (bearer JWT, not a cookie) is inherently CSRF-resistant because the browser will not attach it automatically.

## JWT pitfalls

- **`alg: none` and algorithm confusion** (CWE-347) — a verifier that accepts `alg: none` or that verifies an `RS256`-issued token with `HS256` using the public key as the HMAC secret. Fix: pin the expected algorithm explicitly in the verify call; never derive it from the token's own header.
- **No expiry or audience check** (CWE-345) — a token verified for signature only, with `exp`, `aud`, and `iss` never checked, so an old or wrong-service token remains valid indefinitely.
- **Weak or hardcoded signing secret** (CWE-798) — an HS256 secret that is short, guessable, or committed to source; see [secrets](../secrets/SKILL.md).
- **Sensitive claims trusted without re-verification** — a role or price stored in the JWT payload and trusted on every subsequent request instead of re-derived from the database when it changes.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

1: # How this program reports what it found
2: 
3: This worktree is the **report repository**. The code under review is the **target tree**, which is somewhere else on this host: `target.json` beside this file states its absolute path, the files it covers, and the SHA-256 the whole tree locks to.
4: 
5: The target is read-only for every session of this program. `verify-safety-report.mjs` re-hashes every locked file on every run, so a target a department edited fails the program instead of releasing a report about a tree that no longer exists.
6: 
7: ## This file and the skills
8: 
9: When the deployment mounts the code-safety knowledge pack, its `review-method`, `severity-and-evidence` and `report-template` skills own the craft: how to read a codebase, how to score a severity, what evidence has to name, and how the report reads. Follow them.
10: 
11: This file owns what `verify-safety-report.mjs` mechanically decides, and it is binding wherever the two differ in form. There is one such place and it is stated below: the counts each summary carries are written as `- <severity>: <count>` lines so the examiner can compare them with the union, which is the machine-readable form of the skill's "counts per severity".
12: 
13: ## What a department delivers
14: 
15: Two files, both committed on the department's own branch:
16: 
17: - `findings/<department>.json` — a JSON array of findings, `[]` when the department found nothing.
18: - `report/<department>.md` — the department's own prose: what it looked at, what it found, and what it did not reach.
19: 
20: Nothing else. Do not write `SAFETY-REPORT.md`, `findings.json`, `target.json` or `verify-safety-report.mjs`: the first two are the integration's, and the last two are the examiner.
21: 
22: ## The evidence rule
23: 
24: A finding without a file and a line is not a finding. Quote the exact line you cite; `verify-safety-report.mjs` compares your `snippet` with the target's own text at that line, ignoring only whitespace, and refuses the whole file when they differ.
25: 
26: Prefer three findings you have read the code for over twelve a pattern matched. `confidence` is what you actually know: `confirmed` when you read the sink, the source and the path between them; `likely` when the sink is dangerous and the source is plausibly attacker-controlled; `possible` when the pattern is there and the reachability is not established.
27: 
28: ## The finding
29: 
30: ```json
31: {
32:   "id": "secrets-cookie-secret",
33:   "cwe": "CWE-798",
34:   "owasp": "A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures",
35:   "severity": "high",
36:   "confidence": "confirmed",
37:   "title": "Session cookie secret is hard-coded in the committed configuration",
38:   "file": "config/env/all.js",
39:   "line": 8,
40:   "snippet": "cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\",",
41:   "evidence": "The value is a literal in a committed file and is the secret express-session is configured with.",
42:   "impact": "Anyone with the repository can forge a session cookie and authenticate as any user.",
43:   "fix": "Read the secret from the environment and rotate the committed value.",
44:   "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html"]
45: }
46: ```
47: 
48: | Field | Rule |
49: | --- | --- |
50: | `id` | letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, unique across the whole program; prefix it with your department or use the pack's `SEC-<n>` numbering. |
51: | `cwe` | `CWE-<number>`. |
52: | `owasp` | the OWASP Top 10 category, named. |
53: | `severity` | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` or `info`. |
54: | `confidence` | `confirmed`, `likely` or `possible`. |
55: | `title` | one line a reader can act on. |
56: | `file` | path relative to the target root, exactly as `target.json` lists it. |
57: | `line` | 1-based line in that file. |
58: | `endLine` | optional last line when the finding spans several; `snippet` then quotes all of them. |
59: | `snippet` | the target's own text at those lines, verbatim. |
60: | `evidence` | why this line is the vulnerability, naming what you read. |
61: | `impact` | what an attacker gets. |
62: | `fix` | what to change. |
63: | `references` | array of URLs or identifiers; may be empty. |
64: 
65: ## Checking your own work before you commit
66: 
67: ```sh
68: node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/<department>.json
69: ```
70: 
71: That is the same command your goal is measured by. Run it, fix what it names, then commit everything — work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured.
72: 
73: ## What the integration delivers
74: 
75: The integration merges every department branch and then writes two files of its own.
76: 
77: `findings.json` is the union of every `findings/<department>.json`, deduplicated by `file` + `line` + `cwe`, keeping the entry with the higher `confidence`. Before writing it, ask the examiner which findings do not hold:
78: 
79: ```sh
80: for f in findings/*.json; do node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings "$f" --list-invalid; done
81: ```
82: 
83: Every id that command prints is dropped from `findings.json` and named under `## What was not covered`, with the reason the examiner gave. Dropping one silently fails the report: `--report` refuses a union that omits an id no section discloses.
84: 
85: `SAFETY-REPORT.md` carries exactly these sections, in this order:
86: 
87: ```markdown
88: ## Résumé exécutif
89: 
90: <deux paragraphes en français : ce qui a été examiné, ce qui a été trouvé, ce que cela implique>
91: 
92: - critical: 0
93: - high: 0
94: - medium: 0
95: - low: 0
96: - info: 0
97: 
98: ## Executive summary
99: 
100: <the same in English>
101: 
102: - critical: 0
103: - high: 0
104: - medium: 0
105: - low: 0
106: - info: 0
107: 
108: ## Scope and method
109: 
110: <the target, its locked file count, which departments ran, which tools ran — the scanner, the advisory source — and which files were actually read>
111: 
112: ## Findings
113: 
114: ### critical
115: 
116: - `<id>` — <title> (`<file>:<line>`, <cwe>, <confidence>) — <impact, then fix>
117: 
118: ### high
119: 
120: ...
121: 
122: ## What was not covered
123: 
124: - <a department, a file kind, a class of vulnerability, or a check that did not run, and why>
125: - <every dropped finding id, with the examiner's reason>
126: 
127: ## Certificate
128: 
129: Verified findings: <count>
130: Target tree: <the sha256 from target.json>
131: 
132: <one sentence on what was checked mechanically: that every finding resolves to a real file and line in the locked tree, that every id is unique, and that no two findings share file, line and CWE>
133: 
134: This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".
135: ```
136: 
137: Both summary sections state a `- <severity>: <count>` line for all five severities, and the five counts must be the counts `findings.json` actually holds. Every finding id in `findings.json` is cited in `## Findings`. Every `<file>:<line>` written anywhere in the report must resolve in the target, so write a path you did not read as prose rather than as a citation.
138: 
139: The report is a review by a language model, grounded by a static scanner and by this examiner. Say so in `## Scope and method`. Never write that the target is secure, safe, or free of vulnerabilities: `verify-safety-report.mjs` refuses those claims, because nothing this program did could support one.
140: 
141: Check it before you commit:
142: 
143: ```sh
144: node verify-safety-report.mjs --report
145: ```

(End of file - total 145 lines)

2:  * Out-of-process ACP subagent backend. Each child has its own process, session, model, and
3:  * tools, so it shares no Cordis context and advertises no parent-enforced start capabilities;
4:  * the ONE thing it reads off `request.parent` is the session's workspace cwd (see
5:  * {@link resolveCwd}). This plugin uses named exports only; a default would hide its
6:  * loader metadata (see `docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md`).

8:  */

25: export const inject = ['subagents', 'subprocess']

28: export interface Config {
29:   /** Provider name on `ctx.subagents` (default `acp`). */
30:   providerName: string
31:   /** The executable to spawn for each run (the child ACP agent). */
32:   command: string
33:   /** Arguments passed to {@link command}. */
34:   args: string[]
35:   /**
36:    * Working directory override for the child process and its ACP session.
37:    * Must be non-empty; a relative path resolves against the harness launch
38:    * directory at load, and the result must be an existing directory. When
39:    * omitted, each child inherits its delegating parent session's cwd — and
40:    * starting one from a parent session that has no cwd fails.
41:    */
42:   cwd?: string
43:   /**
44:    * How to auto-answer the child's `session/request_permission` prompts:
45:    * `reject` (default — decline every prompt) or `allow` (approve via the first
46:    * `allow_once` or `allow_always` option). No prompt is surfaced to a human.
47:    */
48:   permission: PermissionPolicy
49:   /**
50:    * Extra environment variables for the child process — e.g. the child
51:    * harness's own `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. Forwarded on top of a credential-scrubbed
52:    * copy of the parent env, so an explicit key here reaches the child while
53:    * ambient secrets do not leak implicitly.
54:    */
55:   env: Record<string, string>
56:   /**
57:    * Grace period (ms) for the child's EOF-driven quiesce on dispose — its
58:    * window to flush persistence and tear down its own nested subprocesses
59:    * before the parent escalates to a signal. Must not exceed
60:    * `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`.
61:    */
62:   disposeEofGraceMs?: number
63:   /** Termination-escalation grace (ms); must not exceed `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`. */
64:   disposeGraceMs?: number
65: }
66: 
67: export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({
68:   providerName: z.string().default('acp'),
69:   command: z.string().required(),
70:   args: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
71:   cwd: z.string(),
72:   permission: z.union(['allow', 'reject'] as const).default('reject'),
73:   env: z.dict(z.string()).default({}),
74:   disposeEofGraceMs: z.number().default(DEFAULT_DISPOSE_EOF_GRACE_MS),
75:   disposeGraceMs: z.number().default(DEFAULT_DISPOSE_GRACE_MS),
76: })

78: /** A dispose grace must fit the single Node timer that owns its teardown tier. */
79: function assertPositiveFinite(name: string, value: number): void {
80:   if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0 || value > MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS) {
81:     throw new Error(`subagent-acp: ${name} must be a positive finite number no greater than ${MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS}`)
82:   }
83: }

85: /** The shape after schemastery applied the defaults (cwd has none). */
86: type ResolvedConfig = Required<Omit<Config, 'cwd'>> & Pick<Config, 'cwd'>
87: 
88: /**
89:  * Whether `path` names an existing directory the harness can ENTER. The
90:  * search-permission probe matters: `statSync().isDirectory()` is true for a
91:  * mode-600 directory, but a subprocess cwd needs `X_OK` or spawn fails EACCES.
92:  */
93: function isDirectory(path: string): boolean {
94:   try {
95:     if (!statSync(path).isDirectory()) return false
96:     accessSync(path, constants.X_OK)
97:     return true
98:   } catch {
99:     // statSync/accessSync throw only filesystem access errors here
100:     // (ENOENT/EACCES/ENOTDIR/…), and every one of them means the path cannot
101:     // serve as the child's cwd.
102:     return false
103:   }
104: }

106: /**
107:  * Assert `cwd` can actually host the child: absolute (it doubles as the ACP
108:  * session workspace, and a relative path would be re-anchored to the server
109:  * process's launch directory) and an existing directory (fail here, before the
110:  * process boundary, instead of as an ambiguous spawn ENOENT).
111:  * @param label - which source supplied the value, for the diagnostic.
112:  * @param cwd - the candidate working directory.
113:  * @returns `cwd`, validated.
114:  */
115: function assertUsableCwd(label: string, cwd: string): string {
116:   if (!isAbsolute(cwd)) {
117:     throw new Error(`subagent-acp: ${label} must be an absolute path: ${cwd}`)
118:   }
119:   if (!isDirectory(cwd)) {
120:     throw new Error(`subagent-acp: ${label} is not an accessible directory: ${cwd}`)
121:   }
122:   return cwd
123: }
124: 
125: /**
126:  * Resolve the child's working directory: the deployment `cwd` override when
127:  * configured (already validated at load), else the parent session's workspace
128:  * cwd (validated here, its earliest resolvable point). Fails loud when neither
129:  * exists — falling back to the harness process cwd would silently bind the
130:  * child to the server's launch directory instead of the delegating session's
131:  * workspace (one server process serves many sessions, each with its own cwd).
132:  */
133: function resolveCwd(configured: string | undefined, request: SubagentStartRequest): string {
134:   if (configured !== undefined) return configured
135:   const parentCwd = request.parent.session.header.cwd
136:   if (parentCwd === undefined) {
137:     throw new Error('subagent-acp: no working directory for the child — configure `cwd` or delegate from a parent session that has one')
138:   }
139:   return assertUsableCwd('parent session cwd', parentCwd)
140: }
141: 
142: /**
143:  * The ACP provider. Advertises NO start-time capabilities: an out-of-process
144:  * child cannot honor `outputSchema`/`maxDepth`/`toolFilter` (the service rejects
145:  * a request needing any of them before `start` runs), and the protocol's
146:  * `session/new` carries no model selection, so `model` is refused there too
147:  * rather than accepted and left to the agent's own configuration.
148:  */
149: class AcpProvider implements SubagentProvider {
150:   readonly capabilities: SubagentCapabilities = {
151:     outputSchema: false, depthLimit: false, toolFilter: false, persona: false, harnessTools: false, model: false,
152:   }
153:   // Context contract: an out-of-process ACP child starts fresh — no parent conversation crosses the process boundary.
154:   readonly inheritsParentContext = false
155: 
156:   constructor(readonly name: string, private readonly ctx: Context, private readonly config: ResolvedConfig) {}
157: 
158:   start(request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest) {
159:     assertOutOfProcessAllowed(this.ctx, request.parent)
160:     const spec: AcpRunSpec = {
161:       command: this.config.command,
162:       args: this.config.args,
163:       cwd: resolveCwd(this.config.cwd, request),
164:       permission: this.config.permission,
165:       env: this.config.env,
166:       disposeEofGraceMs: this.config.disposeEofGraceMs,
167:       disposeGraceMs: this.config.disposeGraceMs,
168:       spawn: spec => this.ctx.subprocess.spawn(spec),
169:       onError: (error, stopReason) => {
170:         // The seam forbids `result` rejecting, so a child-level failure is
171:         // flattened to a stop reason — preserve it here rather than losing it.
172:         this.ctx.logger.warn(`subagent-acp "${this.name}": child run failed (${stopReason}): ${error.message}`)
173:       },
174:     }
175:     return startAcpRun(request, spec)
176:   }
177: }
178: 
179: export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
180:   // schemastery (Config) has already filled every defaulted field.
181:   const resolved = config as ResolvedConfig
182:   assertPositiveFinite('disposeEofGraceMs', resolved.disposeEofGraceMs)
183:   assertPositiveFinite('disposeGraceMs', resolved.disposeGraceMs)
184:   // `path.resolve('')` is the process cwd — an empty string would silently
185:   // reintroduce the launch-directory fallback this resolution removed.
186:   if (resolved.cwd === '') {
187:     throw new Error('subagent-acp: config cwd must not be empty — omit the key to inherit the parent session cwd')
188:   }
189:   // Interpret a relative configured cwd against the harness launch directory
190:   // ONCE, at load, and fail a misconfigured directory here — not per start.
191:   const validated: ResolvedConfig = resolved.cwd === undefined
192:     ? resolved
193:     : { ...resolved, cwd: assertUsableCwd('config cwd', resolve(resolved.cwd)) }
194:   ctx.subagents.registerProvider(new AcpProvider(validated.providerName, ctx, validated))
195:   enforceOutOfProcessRefusal(ctx)
196: }

55:   const record = usage as Record<string, unknown>

113:   if (message.type !== 'assistant') return undefined

153:   readonly agent: Agent

155:   readonly id: SessionId

194: }

197: interface BridgeEventMap {
198:   'bridge/start': BridgeStartData
199:   'bridge/assistant': BridgeAssistantData
200:   'bridge/end': BridgeEndData
201: }

203: /**
204:  * Narrow the generic append face to this package's own events, which
205:  * discharges `Session.append`'s conditional surface-options tuple: all three
206:  * are log-only.
207:  * @param session - the child session recording the run.
208:  * @returns the narrowed append function.
209:  */
210: function bridgeRecorder(session: Session) {
211:   return session.append.bind(session) as <Event extends keyof BridgeEventMap>(
212:     event: Event,
213:     value: SessionEventMap[Event],
214:   ) => void
215: }

217: /**
218:  * Create the child harness agent, serve its tools, and open the run's durable
219:  * record. Rejection leaves nothing published: the agent factory's creation
220:  * transaction rolls back, and a failure after publication releases the child
221:  * before rethrowing.
222:  * @param inputs - the provider context, the resolved request, and the provider name.
223:  * @returns the live bridge the run is driven through.
224:  */
225: export async function openBridgedRun(inputs: BridgeInputs): Promise<BridgedRun> {
226:   const { ctx, request, provider } = inputs
227:   const toolServer = requireToolServer(ctx)
228:   const parent = request.parent
229:   const childDepth = resolveChildDepth(parent, request.maxDepth)
230:   const childId = SessionId(randomUUID())
231:   // Captured before the first await: a later parent switch belongs to the
232:   // parent's future, not to this child.
233:   const inherited = captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides(parent)
234: 
235:   const handle: AgentHandle = await parent.ctx.agents.create({
236:     sessionId: childId,
237:     meta: childSessionMeta(parent, childDepth, 0),
238:     agentOptions: resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, request.agentOptions, childDepth),
239:     signal: request.signal,
240:     setup: (childCtx: Context): void => {
241:       appendDelegatedPolicyOverrides((childCtx.agent as Agent).session, inherited)
242:       // The composition carries no per-child persona or tool filter: this
243:       // provider advertises neither capability, so the service has already
244:       // rejected a request that asked for one.
245:       applyChildComposition(childCtx, parent, {})
246:       ;(childCtx.agent as Agent).session.append('subagent/descriptor', request.descriptor)
247:     },
248:   })
249: 
250:   const agent = handle.agent
251:   let served: McpToolServerHandle
252:   try {
253:     served = toolServer.instance(agent, { serverName: BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME })
254:   } catch (error: unknown) {
255:     await handle.dispose()
256:     throw error
257:   }
258: 
259:   const record = bridgeRecorder(agent.session)
260:   record('bridge/start', {
261:     provider,
262:     tools: served.toolNames.map(name => `${BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX}${name}`),
263:   })
264: 
265:   let settled = false
266:   let lastUsage: TokenUsage | undefined
267:   let lastModel: string | undefined
268:   let lastCostUsd: number | undefined
269:   let released: Promise<void> | undefined
270:   const settle = (stopReason: SubagentStopReason): void => {
271:     if (settled) return
272:     settled = true
273:     record('bridge/end', {
274:       stopReason,
275:       ...lastUsage === undefined ? {} : { usage: lastUsage },
276:       ...lastModel === undefined ? {} : { model: lastModel },
277:       ...lastCostUsd === undefined ? {} : { costUsd: lastCostUsd },
278:     })
279:   }
280: 
281:   return {
282:     agent,
283:     id: childId,
284:     options: bridgeQueryOptions(served.config, request.agentOptions?.maxTurns),
285:     observe(message: SDKMessage): void {
286:       lastModel = initReportedModel(message) ?? lastModel
287:       lastUsage = resultReportedUsage(message) ?? lastUsage
288:       lastCostUsd = resultReportedCostUsd(message) ?? lastCostUsd
289:       const assistant = bridgeAssistantRecord(message)
290:       if (assistant !== undefined) record('bridge/assistant', assistant)
291:     },
292:     settle,
293:     release(): Promise<void> {
294:       if (released !== undefined) return released
295:       // The run's record closes before the served turn does, so `bridge/end`
296:       // always lands inside the turn its tool calls occupy.
297:       settle('aborted')
298:       released = served.dispose().then(() => handle.dispose())
299:       return released
300:     },
301:   }
302: }

46:  * same two deployment-owned fields without adding a shared config owner. */
47: /** Deployment-owned environment, process-release bound, and product permission policy. */
48: export interface Config {

50:    * Explicit environment entries layered over the subprocess seam's

52:    */
53:   env?: Record<string, string>
54:   /** Grace in milliseconds for Claude Code process-tree termination. */

56:   /**

90:    * identifier it does not accept instead of running another one.
91:    */

94:     harnessTools: true,
95:     model: true,
96:   }

101:     private readonly config: ResolvedConfig,
102:   ) {}

104:   async start(request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest) {

106:     const parentCwd = request.parent.session.header.cwd

109:         'subagent-claude-code: no working directory for the child — delegate from a parent session that has one',

113:       'claude',
114:       this.config.env,
115:       request.signal,
116:     )
117:     const bridge = request.harnessTools === undefined
118:       ? undefined
119:       : await openBridgedRun({ ctx: this.ctx, request, provider: this.name })

121:       cwd: resolveChildCwd(
122:         'subagent-claude-code',
123:         undefined,
124:         parentCwd,
125:       ),
126:       executable,
127:       env: this.config.env,
128:       disposeGraceMs: this.config.disposeGraceMs,
129:       spawn: spawnSpec => this.ctx.subprocess.spawn(spawnSpec),
130:       onError: (error, stopReason) => {

132:           `subagent-claude-code: child run failed (${stopReason}): ${error.message}`,
133:         )
134:       },
135:       ...this.config.permissionMode === undefined ? {} : { permissionMode: this.config.permissionMode },
136:       ...request.model === undefined ? {} : { model: request.model },
137:       // Black-box only: bridge mode serves the harness registry and owns its
138:       // own allowlist, which a deployment list must not widen.
139:       ...bridge === undefined ? { allowedTools: this.config.allowedTools } : { bridge },
140:     }
141:     try {
142:       return await startClaudeCodeRun(request, spec)

144:       // Startup failed after the child agent was published: release it here,
145:       // because no run was returned for the caller to dispose.
146:       await bridge?.release()

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3: // repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4: //
5: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8: //
9: // `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10: // `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11: // stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12: // learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13: //
14: // `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15: // disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16: // findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17: //
18: // Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19: // stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20: // this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22: import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23: import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24: 
25: /** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26: const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27: 
28: /** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29: const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30: 
31: /** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32: const SECTIONS = [
33:   '## Résumé exécutif',
34:   '## Executive summary',
35:   '## Scope and method',
36:   '## Findings',
37:   '## What was not covered',
38:   '## Certificate',
39: ]
40: 
41: /** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42: const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43: 
44: /** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45: const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46: 
47: /** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48: const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49: 
50: /** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51: const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52: 
53: /** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54: const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55: 
56: /** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57: const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61:  * @param {string} root directory to walk
62:  * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63:  * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64:  */
65: function walk(root, exclude) {
66:   const found = []
67:   const descend = (directory) => {
68:     for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69:       const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70:       if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71:         if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72:       } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73:     }
74:   }
75:   descend(root)
76:   return found.sort()
77: }
78: 
79: /** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80: class Target {
81:   /**
82:    * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83:    * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84:    */
85:   constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86:     this.failures = failures
87:     this.root = undefined
88:     this.files = new Map()
89:     this.lines = new Map()
90:     const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91:     if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92:       failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93:       return
94:     }
95:     const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96:     this.root = lock.root
97:     this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98:     this.digest = lock.sha256
99:     for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100:     this.checkTree()
101:   }
102: 
103:   /**
104:    * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105:    * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106:    * department edited is no longer that tree.
107:    */
108:   checkTree() {
109:     if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110:       this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111:       this.root = undefined
112:       return
113:     }
114:     const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115:     for (const path of present) {
116:       if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117:     }
118:     for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119:       if (!present.includes(path)) {
120:         this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121:         continue
122:       }
123:       if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124:         this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: 
129:   /**
130:    * The lines of one target file.
131:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132:    * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133:    */
134:   linesOf(path) {
135:     if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136:     if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137:     return this.lines.get(path)
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143:    * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144:    * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145:    */
146:   resolves(path, line) {
147:     const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148:     return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154:  * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155:  * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157:  * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158:  * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159:  */
160: function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161:   const failures = []
162:   if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163:     return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164:   }
165:   const id = finding.id
166:   const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167:   const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168:   // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169:   // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170:   if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171:   else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172:   else seen.add(id)
173:   if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174:   if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175:   if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176:   if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177:   for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178:     if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179:   }
180:   if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181:     fail('references must be an array of strings')
182:   }
183:   const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184:   if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185:     fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186:     return failures
187:   }
188:   const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189:   if (lines === undefined) {
190:     fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191:     return failures
192:   }
193:   if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194:     fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195:     return failures
196:   }
197:   const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198:   if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199:     fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200:     return failures
201:   }
202:   if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203:     fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204:     return failures
205:   }
206:   const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207:   if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
208:     fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
209:   }
210:   return failures
211: }
212: 
213: /**
214:  * Read one findings file.
215:  * @param {string} path the file to read
216:  * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
217:  * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
218:  */
219: function readFindings(path, failures) {
220:   if (!existsSync(path)) {
221:     failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
222:     return []
223:   }
224:   let parsed
225:   try {
226:     parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
227:   } catch (error) {
228:     failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
229:     return []
230:   }
231:   if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
232:     failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
233:     return []
234:   }
235:   return parsed
236: }
237: 
238: /**
239:  * Decide one findings file on its own.
240:  * @param {string} path the findings file
241:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
242:  * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
243:  */
244: function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
245:   const failures = []
246:   const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
247:   const invalid = []
248:   const seen = new Set()
249:   findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
250:     const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
251:     if (broken.length === 0) return
252:     failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
253:     invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
254:   })
255:   return { failures, invalid, findings }
256: }
257: 
258: /**
259:  * The body of one section of the report.
260:  * @param {string} text the whole report
261:  * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
262:  * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
263:  */
264: function section(text, heading) {
265:   const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
266:   if (start === -1) return ''
267:   const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
268:   const next = body.search(/^## /m)
269:   return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
270: }
271: 
272: /**
273:  * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
274:  * @param {string} root the report repository
275:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
276:  * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
277:  */
278: function checkReport(root, target) {
279:   const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
280:   if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
281:     return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
282:   }
283:   const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
284:   const failures = []
285:   let previous = -1
286:   for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
287:     const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
288:     if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
289:     else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
290:     else previous = at
291:   }
292:   const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
293:   if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
294:   const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
295:   if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
296:

// repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
// `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
// `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
// stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
// learns which findings to drop and disclose.
// `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
// disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
// findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
// Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
// stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
// this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
/** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
/** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
/** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
/** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */

const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
/** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
/** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
* Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
* @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
/** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
* @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
* @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
* Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
* cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
* department edited is no longer that tree.

if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)

* @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id

// numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')

if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')

fail('references must be an array of strings')
const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)

fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
* @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
* @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
* Decide one findings file on its own.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
* @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
* The body of one section of the report.
* @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
* @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
* Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
// The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
// the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')
else if (tree[1] !== target.digest) failures.push(`the Certificate states target tree ${tree[1]}, and target.json locks ${target.digest}`)

// section: requiring a finding would buy one by inventing it.
if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified against ${target.root}`)

## Scope and method

Target tree: `/home/user/enterprise-scratch/dsh-subagent-providers/repo` (locked in `target.json`, sha256 `a2da992332d755dcdd20b89b8fac7ca936580e1ee450ed766c9c5e96649a592f`), 24 files under `packages/subagent/{subagent-acp,subagent-claude-code,subagent-codex,subagent-dsh-sdk}`.

`semgrep --version` reported `1.177.0`, so semgrep ran: `semgrep --config <local code-safety pack> --config p/owasp-top-ten --metrics off --json` over the target root. The registry pack (`p/owasp-top-ten`) downloaded successfully. The scan covered all 24 files with 89 rules and reported 2 findings, both `dsh-eval-on-input` hits on `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/src/bridge.ts:60` and `packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/wire.ts:325` — an `eval()` call on data read off a child process's protocol stream. Both are code-injection patterns (CWE-95), not an authentication/session/authorization pattern, so they are out of this department's scope and are not reported here as access findings; they are read and disclosed under "What was not covered" for the injection department to pick up. Every semgrep hit was read, not filed as a finding on the hit alone, per instructions.

Every one of the 24 locked files was opened and read in full: all `src/*.ts` in the four packages (`index.ts`, `run.ts`, `invariant.ts` in every package, plus `bridge.ts`, `process.ts`, `types.ts` in `subagent-claude-code`, and `wire.ts` in `subagent-codex`), all four `README.md`, and all four `package.json`. Targeted greps for `role|admin|isAdmin|permission|Permission|trust|auth|Auth` and for `token|secret|password|serviceToken|DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN` were run across the whole target tree to confirm there was no unread reference to any of those terms outside the files already opened.

## What this codebase is

This target is not a web application. It is a set of internal Cordis plugins ("subagent providers") that each spawn one child process (an ACP agent, the Claude Code CLI via the Agent SDK, the Codex app-server, or another DeepSeek Harness runtime) to run one delegated task, then tear the child down. There is no HTTP route, no browser-facing login, no password, no cookie, and no CSRF-relevant form in these 24 files. Most of the categories this department normally hunts — account enumeration in a login/signup flow, a password-policy validator, session-cookie flags, CSRF tokens on state-changing routes, session fixation/expiry at web-login — have no code surface in this tree to find them in, and are recorded as not applicable below rather than reported as absent findings (an absent web-login surface is not the same claim as a checked-and-passing web-login surface).

The one boundary that does map onto "authorization, route by route" here is each provider's `start()` entry point, which is the equivalent of a route handler: it is the single place every one of the four providers accepts a `SubagentStartRequest`/`ResolvedSubagentStartRequest` and turns it into a spawned child process. I traced each one:

- `packages/subagent/subagent-acp/src/index.ts:159` — `start()` calls `assertOutOfProcessAllowed(this.ctx, request.parent)` as its first statement, before `resolveCwd` or `startAcpRun`.
- `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/src/index.ts:105` — same call, same position, before resolving `parentCwd` or spawning.
- `packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/index.ts:66` — same call, same position.
- `packages/subagent/subagent-dsh-sdk/src/index.ts:110` — same call, same position.

All four "routes" open with the same authorization gate before doing anything else, and `assertOutOfProcessAllowed`/`enforceOutOfProcessRefusal` are called consistently in every provider's `start()`/`apply()`. I did not find a fifth entry point that skips this call. (`assertOutOfProcessAllowed` itself is implemented in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent`, which is outside the 24 locked files — its own correctness is not something this review can certify from this tree, and is named under "What was not covered".) I looked for a caller-settable privilege (a `role`/`isAdmin`/permission field on the request that the request itself could escalate) and found none: the only caller-influenced knobs are `model` and `harnessTools`/`maxTurns`, gated by each provider's static, hard-coded `capabilities` object rather than by anything the request can set for itself. Default *policy* choices are conservative where they exist: `subagent-acp`'s `permission` config defaults to `'reject'` (line `subagent-acp/src/index.ts:72`), and Codex's unattended approval handler in `wire.ts` defaults to `'decline'`/empty permission grants rather than allow.

## Findings

Two findings, both CWE-798 (use of hard-coded credentials), one per file — see `findings/access.json` for the full records.

- `access-hardcoded-service-token-claude-code` — `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/src/run.ts:45`: `const serviceToken44 = process.env.DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN || 'ef2226e36ddae1fb2d5292e0ce927f23'`. A service-authentication token variable whose value silently falls back to a fixed literal committed to source when the environment variable is absent.
- `access-hardcoded-service-token-codex` — `packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/run.ts:26`: `const serviceToken25 = process.env.DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN || '4763278f0e9a2a62c9580300cf64c2c6'`. The same pattern, a different literal, in the sibling package.

I read every other line of both files, and of every file that imports from them, to check whether either variable is ever read again: it is not. Neither `serviceToken44` nor `serviceToken25` is referenced anywhere else in the 24 locked files (confirmed by a repo-wide grep for `serviceToken` and for `DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN`, which returns only these two declaration lines). That is why severity is `low` rather than `high`: there is no reachable sink in this tree today that an attacker could drive with this value, so this is not an active authentication bypass as read. It is still a genuine CWE-798 instance — a real secret-shaped default is committed to source control, unconditionally, with no warning when the environment variable is missing — and it is exactly the shape of default credential that turns into a live bypass the moment either variable is wired into an actual check, or if a sibling service elsewhere keys off the same `DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN` convention and receives this same well-known fallback. Confidence is `confirmed` for the literal itself (both lines were read verbatim); the "currently unused" qualifier is stated plainly here and in each finding's evidence so severity, not confidence, carries that nuance.

## What was not covered

- **Account enumeration, password policy, session-cookie flags/fixation/expiry, and CSRF on state-changing routes** — not applicable to this tree: none of the 24 files contains a login, signup, password-reset, or HTTP-cookie-backed session. This is a statement about the absence of that surface, not a claim that such a surface was checked and found safe.
- **`assertOutOfProcessAllowed` / `enforceOutOfProcessRefusal`** (imported from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent`) — every provider's `start()`/`apply()` calls these consistently and first, but their own implementation lives outside the 24 locked files this review's target covers, so their correctness (whether the check they perform is actually sufficient) was not verified here.
- **`SubagentStartRequest`/`ResolvedSubagentStartRequest` and the shared `dsh-subagent` package** — the type that carries `parent`, `model`, `harnessTools`, `maxTurns` and `signal` is defined outside this tree; whether any of its fields are attacker-reachable from outside the harness process was not established from these 24 files alone.
- **`packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/src/bridge.ts:60`** (`eval(String(cacheRead))`) and **`packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/wire.ts:325`** (`eval(String(turn))`) — both read, both semgrep hits, both code-injection (CWE-95) on data read from a child process stream rather than an authentication/authorization defect; left for the injection department rather than filed here.
- **Dependency and supply-chain review of the four `package.json` files** — read for content, not audited for known-vulnerable versions; that is the dependencies department's remit.
- **Runtime/deployment configuration** — how `DSH_SERVICE_TOKEN` (or the absence of it) is actually set in any real deployment was not observable from static source alone.
"}
